title: Hungary and Slovakia suspend diesel exports to Ukraine over Druzhba pipeline dispute
body:
On 18 February 2026, Hungary and Slovakia announced that they would suspend diesel exports to Ukraine. Russian oil deliveries to both countries through the Druzhba pipeline had stopped on 27 January 2026. Media reports said a Russian air strike had damaged the pipeline on Ukrainian territory.

Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto said diesel deliveries would not resume until Ukraine resumed crude oil deliveries to Hungary. He said Ukraine had enough means and time to repair the pipeline and was making a political decision not to do so. In Slovakia, the government of Prime Minister Robert Fico said the state-controlled Slovnaft refinery would stop exporting diesel to Ukraine and other destinations. Slovakia also released 250,000 tonnes of oil from its emergency reserves.

Both countries said they had sufficient fuel reserves. They asked the European Commission to allow Russian crude to be transported through Croatian ports, but Croatia rejected the request, saying it could violate American sanctions. On 17 February, the European Commission had said that the energy security of Hungary and Slovakia was not at risk because of sufficient reserves. Ukraine was at the time facing a severe energy crisis after Russian strikes damaged its infrastructure during winter.
